answer:
Newton’s law of cooling gives  
\[
T(t)-20=(T(0)-20)e^{-kt}.
\]
With \(T(0)=80\) and \(T(12)=50\),
\[
50-20=(80-20)e^{-12k}
\]
so
\[
\frac12=e^{-12k}\quad\Rightarrow\quad k=\frac{\ln 2}{12}.
\]

After a further \(18\) minutes, \(t=30\):
\[
T(30)-20=60e^{-30k}
=60\left(2^{-30/12}\right)
=60\cdot 2^{-5/2}
\approx 10.607.
\]
Thus
\[
T(30)\approx 20+10.607=\boxed{30.6^\circ\text{C}}.
\]

To reach \(25^\circ\)C:
\[
25-20=60e^{-kt}
\]
\[
e^{-kt}=\frac{1}{12}
\]
\[
t=\frac{\ln 12}{k}
=12\frac{\ln 12}{\ln 2}
=12\log_2 12
\approx 43.02\text{ min}.
\]
So it reaches \(25^\circ\)C after about \(\boxed{43.0\text{ min}}\) from the start, i.e. about \(31.0\) minutes after the 12-minute reading. It is below \(25^\circ\)C immediately after that time.

The average cooling rate over the first 12 minutes is
\[
\frac{80-50}{12}=2.5^\circ\text{C/min}.
\]
If this constant average rate were extrapolated for another 18 minutes, the temperature would be
\[
50-2.5(18)=50-45=5^\circ\text{C},
\]
which is below room temperature and therefore impossible. So extrapolating the first average cooling rate is **not consistent** with Newton’s law; the cooling rate decreases as the temperature approaches \(20^\circ\)C.

\[
\boxed{T(30)\approx 30.6^\circ\text{C},\quad T=25^\circ\text{C at }t\approx 43.0\text{ min}.}
\]
